question.text: Special Situation Fund (SSF) under AIF Regulations is registered as a sub-category under which AIF category, and which Insolvency framework does Chapter 9 specifically mention it can participate in as a Resolution Applicant?

answer.text: Sub-category under Cat III; under the SARFAESI Act only.
Sub-category under Category I AIF; may act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016.
Standalone category; only under RBI's Prudential Framework.
Sub-category under Cat II; under the Companies Act, 2013 only.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'Under the AIF Regulations, special situations fund is a sub-category under Category I AIF and has to be registered as such. Special Situation Fund means a Category I AIF that invests in special situation assets in accordance with its investment objectives and may act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016.' The Trap: Option A assigns to Cat III (wrong — SSF is Cat I). Option C makes it standalone. Option D assigns to Cat II. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-A test SSF classification. Chapter 14 (SEBI AIF Regulations in detail) expands on SSF economics. III-A/C covers IBC resolution-applicant eligibility. Manager's Pro-Tip: When registering an SSF, maintain the specific sub-category registration — do not attempt to execute stressed-asset trades under a generic Cat I or Cat II licence, as SEBI enforcement has treated category drift strictly. Also, coordinate with IBC Board certifications for key personnel.
